t.1.13.1: Then, when a full year had passed and that horse had returned, the king's sacrifice began on the northern bank of the Sarayū.
t.1.13.2: Placing Ṛṣyaśṛṅga at their head, the foremost of the twice-born performed the rites in the great sacrifice, the Aśvamedha, of this most high-souled king.
t.1.13.3: The officiating priests, masters of the Vedas, perform the rites according to rule; in keeping with the prescribed ordinance and with propriety, they move about in accordance with the scriptures.
t.1.13.4: Having performed the Pravargya according to the scriptures, and likewise the Upasad, the twice-born priests duly carried out all the further rites as prescribed by the scriptures.
t.1.13.5: Then, having offered their worship, all the foremost of sages, delighted, performed according to rule the rites that begin with the morning soma-pressing.
t.1.13.6: Nothing there went unoffered, nor was there any slip whatsoever; everything is seen to be in accordance with the sacred mantras, for they performed it all with care for its safe and auspicious completion.
t.1.13.7: During those days no one was seen there who was weary or hungry; nor was there any brāhmaṇa who was unlearned, nor any who lacked a hundred followers.
t.1.13.9: The aged and the sick, women and children as well, though they ate without ceasing, were not seen to reach satiety.
t.1.13.8: The brāhmaṇas are fed continually, and those who have protectors are fed; the ascetics are fed as well, and the śramaṇas are fed likewise.
t.1.13.10: "Let food be given, let it be given, and garments of many kinds!" Thus urged there, they did so again and again.
t.1.13.11: And there, day after day, many heaps of food resembling mountains were then seen, prepared according to due rule.
t.1.13.12: The foremost of the twice-born praised the food, properly prepared and delicious, and Rāghava heard them say, "Ah, we are satisfied; may good fortune be yours!"
t.1.13.13: Well-adorned men served food to the brāhmaṇas, while others, wearing brightly polished jewelled earrings, waited upon them.
t.1.13.14: Then, in the intervals between the rites, the wise and highly eloquent brāhmaṇas put forward many arguments of reasoning, each eager to defeat the other.
t.1.13.15: Day after day, there at the sacrificial ground, the skilled twice-born, urged on in accordance with the scriptures, performed all the rites.
t.1.13.16: There was no twice-born priest among the assembly of that king who did not know the six Vedāṅgas, who was without vows, who was not deeply learned, or who was unskilled in debate.
t.1.13.17: When the time came for raising the sacrificial posts, six were of bilva wood and likewise six of khadira; as many more stood together with the bilva posts, and still others were likewise of parṇin wood.
t.1.13.19: All of these were caused to be made by those learned in the śāstras and skilled in sacrifice, and for the splendour of that sacrifice they were adorned with gold.
t.1.13.18: One post made of śleṣmātaka wood was prescribed, and likewise one made of devadāru; just these two were set up there, placed an outstretched arm-span apart.
t.1.13.21: Clothed in garments and adorned with flowers and perfumes, they shone resplendent, like the radiant Seven Sages in the sky.
t.1.13.20: All of them were set up according to rule, well made and sturdy, by the craftsmen; every one of them was eight-sided and smooth in form.
t.1.13.22: Bricks were made in the proper manner and according to the prescribed measure, and there the fire-altar was built by brāhmaṇas skilled in the rules of the śulba measurements. That fire-altar of the lion among kings, which was to be piled, was carefully built up by skilled twice-born priests.
t.1.13.23: There was a Garuḍa with golden wings, threefold and made up of eighteen parts, and there the sacrificial animals were bound, each one dedicated to its own particular deity.
t.1.13.25: All of this was then arranged by the priests in accordance with the scriptures; three hundred animals were then tied there to the sacrificial posts, together with the finest jewel of horses belonging to King Daśaratha.
t.1.13.24: Serpents and birds, as the scriptures prescribe, were brought forward there to the place of immolation, and so too the horse and the creatures that dwell in the water.
t.1.13.26: Kausalyā, having attended upon that horse there on every side, cut it with three swords with the greatest joy.
t.1.13.29: The priest, self-restrained and supremely accomplished, drew out the omentum of that bird and cooked it according to the scriptures.
t.1.13.28: The Hotṛ, the Adhvaryu and likewise the Udgātṛ joined with the horse the chief queen and the neglected queen, and then likewise the other, the favourite queen.
t.1.13.30: The lord of men inhaled the smell of the smoke of the omentum at the proper time and in accordance with the rule, thereby dispelling his own sin.
t.1.13.31: And whatever limbs of the horse there were, all of them the brāhmaṇas, the sixteen officiating priests together, offered into the fire according to the prescribed rite.
t.1.13.32: For other sacrifices the oblation is prepared on branches of the plakṣa tree, but for the aśvamedha alone a portion of vaitasa cane is prescribed.
t.1.13.33: The Aśvamedha is reckoned by the brāhmaṇas, according to the Kalpasūtra, as a rite of three days; its first day was arranged as the Catuṣṭoma.
t.1.13.27: Then Kausalyā, with a steadfast mind and out of desire for dharma, dwelt for one night together with the bird.
t.1.13.34: The second day was reckoned as the Ukthya, and likewise the one after it as the Atirātra. Many rites were performed there, prescribed in accordance with the teaching of the śāstras.
t.1.13.35: The Jyotiṣṭoma and the Āyus were performed, and the two Atirātras as well; the Abhijit and the Viśvajit too, and the Aptoryāma, the great sacrifice.
t.1.13.36: The king, who increased the glory of his own lineage, gave the eastern quarter to the Hotṛ priest, the western to the Adhvaryu, and the southern quarter to the Brahman priest.
t.1.13.38: Then, having duly completed the sacrifice according to rule, the king, bull among men and promoter of sacrifices, gave that earth to the officiating priests.
t.1.13.37: And likewise he gave the northern quarter to the udgātṛ; this sacrificial fee was established long ago for the great Aśvamedha sacrifice ordained by Svayambhū.
t.1.13.39: But all the officiating priests said to the king, now freed from sin: "You alone are fit to protect the entire earth."
t.1.13.40: We have no use for land, for we are not able to govern it; we are ever devoted to the study of the Veda, O lord of the earth. Let your honor give us some fitting compensation here instead.
t.1.13.42: Then all the officiating priests together gave wealth to the sage Ṛṣyaśṛṅga and to the wise Vasiṣṭha.
t.1.13.41: The king gave them ten hundred thousand cows, ten crores of gold, and four times as much silver.
t.1.13.43: Then those best of the twice-born, having made the distribution properly, all of them deeply pleased at heart and greatly delighted, replied.
t.1.13.44: Then the king, his mind delighted, having accomplished that unsurpassed sacrifice, which removes sin, leads to heaven, and is hard to achieve even for the bulls among kings,
t.1.13.45: Then King Daśaratha said to Ṛṣyaśṛṅga: "O you of excellent vows, you should perform that rite which is the increase of the lineage."
t.1.13.46: "So be it," said that best of the twice-born to the king. "O king, four sons will be born to you who will carry your lineage forward."
